en: The Sampaguita, the Philippine national flower, is a species of jasmine that blooms year-round and symbolizes purity and simplicity.
The Ifugao people built the Banaue Rice Terraces by carving steps into the mountains and using an ancient gravity-based irrigation system.
Jose Rizal wrote the novels Noli Me Tangere and El Filibusterismo in Spanish to expose the abuses of the Spanish colonial government.
The Philippine government has three co-equal branches: the Legislative makes laws, the Executive enforces them, and the Judiciary interprets them.
During the Sinulog Festival in Cebu, devotees perform a two-steps-forward, one-step-backward dance to honor the Santo Niño.
Filipino, the national language, is primarily based on Tagalog but incorporates words from other native Philippine languages and foreign dialects.
Dr. Fe del Mundo was the first Asian admitted to Harvard Medical School and invented a bamboo incubator for premature babies.
General Emilio Aguinaldo proclaimed Philippine independence from Spain on June 12, 1898, at his home in Kawit, Cavite.
The Carabao, a domesticated swamp buffalo, is the national animal of the Philippines and is essential to traditional Filipino rice farming.
National Artist Juan Luna painted the famous historical artwork Spoliarium, which depicts dying gladiators being dragged away from the arena.
Every Filipino citizen has the constitutional right to vote in national and local elections once they reach the age of eighteen.
The Filipino value of bayanihan involves community members physically helping a family move their traditional nipa hut to a new location.
